name: Fasciolopsiasis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Parasitological Diagnosis of Fasciolopsiasis

criteria.description: Identification of Fasciolopsis buski eggs in stool samples by microscopy
Presence of gastrointestinal symptoms consistent with infection such as abdominal pain and diarrhea
History of ingestion of aquatic plants or contaminated water in endemic areas
Visualization of adult flukes in the small intestine via endoscopy (rarely performed)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Detection of Fasciolopsis buski eggs in stool combined with compatible clinical symptoms and exposure history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Serological tests are not routinely used; diagnosis primarily relies on stool microscopy.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Detection of Fasciolopsis buski eggs in stool
searchTerms: finding intestinal parasite eggs in stool
stool test positive for fluke eggs

pathognomonic.symptomName: Giant intestinal fluke adult worms in small intestine
searchTerms: large intestinal fluke worms in small intestine

common.symptomName: Abdominal pain localized to epigastric and periumbilical regions
searchTerms: belly pain around stomach and navel
reduced food intake and weight drop

occasional.symptomName: Intestinal obstruction due to heavy worm burden
searchTerms: gut obstruction from heavy worm load
fluid buildup due to low protein

occasional.symptomName: Eosinophilia-related symptoms such as rash or pruritus
searchTerms: rash and itching from high eosinophils
itchy rash with high eosinophil count

laboratory: Microscopic identification of Fasciolopsis buski eggs in stool
imaging: Abdominal ultrasound may show intestinal wall thickening
X-ray may reveal signs of intestinal obstruction in heavy infestations
other: History of exposure to contaminated aquatic plants

distinguishingFeatures: Fascioliasis caused by Fasciola hepatica affects liver and bile ducts rather than intestine
Different egg morphology on stool examination
Caused by Entamoeba histolytica with trophozoites in stool rather than eggs
More prominent bloody diarrhea and liver abscesses
Caused by Giardia lamblia with cysts and trophozoites in stool
Usually causes malabsorption and steatorrhea without adult worms
